category: open-access status API for Crossref DOIs; bulk through the OpenAlex snapshot

free_tier.stated: The REST API is free, with up to 100,000 calls per day and an email address as a query parameter; there is no key. Unpaywall no longer makes its own snapshots; the same data is in the OpenAlex public snapshot, free to download from S3 with no AWS account.
free_tier.notes: The 100,000 figure is a stated limit on use, not a measured cutoff; no per-second rate is published. DOI lookup is the only API endpoint: title search was retired on 2026-09-18 and answers 410. Unpaywall runs on the OpenAlex database since late 2025.

per_object_cap.stated: one DOI per API call; the Simple Query Tool takes up to 1,000 DOIs per batch and returns results by email
per_object_cap.notes: Only Crossref DOIs are covered; another DOI answers 404.

retention.stated: the API answers from the live database; Unpaywall snapshots are no longer created; the OpenAlex public snapshot is a point-in-time release, quarterly, on the second Wednesday of January, April, July and October
retention.notes: The Unpaywall snapshot page still says the OpenAlex snapshot is updated approximately once per month; the OpenAlex snapshot page says quarterly for the free public snapshot, and the works listing in the bucket was last modified on 2026-10-14.

egress.terms: Free: API responses carry no byte price; the OpenAlex S3 bucket is free to download with no AWS account, the data-transfer fees covered by the AWS Open Data program

interface_detail: GET https://api.unpaywall.org/v2/{DOI}?email=ADDRESS returns one JSON DOI object; bulk: the OpenAlex bucket s3://openalex/data/ read with --no-sign-request, JSON Lines about 745 GB and Parquet about 770 GB as of the September 2026 release; the paid Data Feed serves daily and weekly changefiles and a daily snapshot with an API key.
tooling: Any HTTP client for the API; the AWS CLI (aws s3 sync with --no-sign-request) or any S3 client for the OpenAlex snapshot.
chaining: Per-DOI lookups go to the Unpaywall API at up to 100,000 a day; a whole-corpus read goes to the OpenAlex public snapshot on S3, whose open_access and best_oa_location fields carry the same values; search goes to the OpenAlex API.

limits.value: 100,000 calls per day; no per-second rate published
one DOI per API call; up to 1,000 DOIs per Simple Query Tool batch

limits_note: A call without an email parameter answered 422. The search endpoint answers 410 since 2026-09-18.
binding_note: At 100,000 calls a day, polling the whole DOI space through the API takes many months, so a whole-corpus read goes to the OpenAlex snapshot, which has no request count.

identity_cost.detail: No account and no key: each call carries an email address as a query parameter, and a call without one answered 422. The example address in the documentation answered 200, so no account stands behind the address. The OpenAlex S3 snapshot needs no AWS account. The Data Feed is paid and priced by quote.

reliability_note: Title search was retired on 2026-09-18 and answers 410; the DOI lookup API and the Data Feed are stated to stay. Unpaywall-format snapshots are no longer made, so a bulk copy is in the OpenAlex format.
confidence_note: The daily figure is documented, not exhausted. A DOI lookup with an email answered 200, one without answered 422, the search endpoint answered 410, and an anonymous listing of the OpenAlex bucket answered 200.
